- pH = 13 (very basic)
- Colorless solution

- OH- (sodium hydroxide - NaOH)
- CO3-2 (sodium carbonate - Na2CO3)
- S-2 (sodium sulfide - Na2S)
- PO4-3 (sodium phosphate - Na3PO4)

Let me test with some reagents to distinguish between these:

1. If it's OH-, adding acid will neutralize it without precipitation
2. If it's CO3-2, adding acid will produce CO2 gas (bubbles)
3. If it's S-2, adding acid will produce H2S gas (rotten egg smell), and it would precipitate many metal cations
4. If it's PO4-3, it would precipitate with many metal cations

Let me test with Ba(NO3)2 first - this will help distinguish:
- OH-: no precipitate
- CO3-2: white precipitate (BaCO3)
- S-2: would give precipitate
- PO4-3: white precipitate (Ba3(PO4)2)
</thought>
